roles.label: Explains
roles.meaning: Source text defines or explains the concept.

roles.label: Demonstrates
roles.meaning: A worked example, figure or formula shows the concept in use.

roles.label: Applies
roles.meaning: A lab, case or scenario requires using the concept.

roles.label: Practices
roles.meaning: A question or drill asks the learner to use the concept; held answers are not used as evidence.

roles.label: References
roles.meaning: Link-only or bibliographic material points at the concept without local full text.

nodes.label: Data quality
nodes.definition: Completeness, validity, uniqueness and consistency checks that decide whether a result can be trusted.
nodes.scope: Fitness of the data; distinct from statistical uncertainty.

nodes.label: Decision frame
nodes.definition: The decision, audience and action that justify an analysis before data or chart choices are made.
nodes.scope: Frames the work; not itself a statistical claim.

nodes.label: Evidence strength
nodes.definition: How much confidence a decision can take from the available data, design and uncertainty.
nodes.scope: Calibrated judgement; not a percentage readiness score.

nodes.label: KPI definition
nodes.definition: A decision metric with an owner, definition, target and leading or lagging behaviour.
nodes.scope: Decision metric; a KPI is not any number on a dashboard.

nodes.label: Metric definition
nodes.definition: A precise numerator, denominator, population and time window for a measure used in a decision.
nodes.scope: Definition discipline; prevents two teams reporting different numbers under one name.

nodes.label: Segmentation
nodes.definition: Comparing defined subgroups while keeping the population and denominator explicit.
nodes.scope: Subgroup comparison; segments must be defined before results are read.

nodes.label: Activator
nodes.definition: A Real-Time Intelligence capability that evaluates conditions on streaming data and triggers actions.
nodes.scope: Condition-to-action alerting; not a scheduled batch refresh.

nodes.label: DAX CALCULATE
nodes.definition: A DAX function that evaluates an expression in a modified filter context.
nodes.scope: Filter-context modification; not a general-purpose row filter.

nodes.label: Capacity
nodes.definition: The compute resource that powers Fabric workloads and bounds what a workspace can run.
nodes.scope: Compute and licensing; not a workspace role or an item permission.

nodes.label: Table clone
nodes.definition: A zero-copy table clone that initially shares data files through copied metadata and diverges as either side changes.
nodes.scope: Initial sharing is not a guarantee of free future storage.

nodes.label: Column-level security
nodes.definition: A permission that restricts selected columns while leaving the rest of the object readable.
nodes.scope: Column projection control; row visibility is a different mechanism.

nodes.label: Pipeline control flow
nodes.definition: Activity sequencing, iteration, conditional routing and metadata discovery inside a data pipeline.
nodes.scope: Orchestration semantics; control flow does not itself transform data and is not the Copy activity's movement contract.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish orchestration from the activity that performs the work.

nodes.label: Copy job
nodes.definition: A Fabric data-movement item that copies data between supported sources and destinations.
nodes.scope: Copy semantics; distinct from referencing a target through a shortcut.

nodes.label: Data masking
nodes.definition: A column-level masking function that changes the value shown to an identity without changing the stored value.
nodes.scope: Presentation masking; UNMASK grants reveal the original value and must be audited.

nodes.label: Database mirroring
nodes.definition: Continuous replication of a supported operational database into Fabric analytical storage.
nodes.scope: Replica, not a reference. Metadata mirroring is a different case.

nodes.label: Dataflow Gen2
nodes.definition: Low-code data preparation using Power Query transformations with a defined output destination.
nodes.scope: Preparation layer; does not replace orchestration or semantic modelling.

nodes.label: Deletion vectors
nodes.definition: Metadata that marks rows deleted without rewriting the underlying Parquet files, subject to reader compatibility.
nodes.scope: Logical deletion metadata; distinct from physical file removal and from time-travel retention.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish a logical delete from a physical rewrite and from a retained historical snapshot.

nodes.label: Delta table
nodes.definition: A table format of Parquet files plus a transaction log that provides schema, history and transactional reads.
nodes.scope: Table format; Delta does not by itself define refresh, security or semantic-model behaviour.

nodes.label: Delta history and time travel
nodes.definition: Delta transaction-log history enables version reads, while VACUUM removes old files and bounds that history.
nodes.scope: History retention. A version can be listed and still be unreadable after file cleanup.

nodes.label: Deployment pipeline
nodes.definition: A staged release mechanism that promotes workspace content across development, test and production stages.
nodes.scope: Release stages; not the same as Git branching or item endorsement.

nodes.label: Direct Lake
nodes.definition: A semantic-model storage mode that reads eligible OneLake Delta data without an Import copy.
nodes.scope: Requires eligible Delta/OneLake conditions; fallback behaviour is a separate decision.

nodes.label: DirectQuery
nodes.definition: A semantic-table storage mode that sends queries to the source at report time instead of storing a copy.
nodes.scope: Source round-trips and source limits constrain the experience.

nodes.label: Dynamic management view
nodes.definition: A live SQL server view of sessions, connections and requests, scoped by workspace role and distinct from retained query history.
nodes.scope: Live operational inspection; not a historical audit log and not a performance score.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish live request state from retained Query Insights history and from role-scoped visibility.

nodes.label: Endorsement
nodes.definition: Promotion or certification that signals an item's review and intended trust level.
nodes.scope: Governance signal; promotion is not the same review bar as certification.

nodes.label: Eventhouse
nodes.definition: A Real-Time Intelligence store for streaming and event data queried with KQL.
nodes.scope: Streaming store; retention and KQL limits are separate constraints.

nodes.label: Eventstream
nodes.definition: A Real-Time Intelligence pipeline that ingests, transforms and routes streaming events to destinations.
nodes.scope: Streaming ingestion and transformation; Eventhouse is a destination/query store.

nodes.label: Pipeline expression language
nodes.definition: The typed expression and dynamic-content system that resolves parameters, activity outputs and run-scoped values before an activity executes.
nodes.scope: Expression evaluation; distinct from a semantic-model DAX expression and from a SQL expression.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish interpolation, typed evaluation and the JSON shape of an activity output.

nodes.label: DAX filter context
nodes.definition: The set of filters active when a DAX expression is evaluated, including filters from visuals and CALCULATE.
nodes.scope: Evaluation context; row context and filter context are not interchangeable.

nodes.label: Gateway
nodes.definition: A bridge that lets Fabric services reach data sources that are not directly reachable from the cloud.
nodes.scope: Connectivity and authentication; gateway type depends on the source and network path.

nodes.label: Git integration
nodes.definition: Version control of workspace items through a connected Git repository, including branch and commit behaviour.
nodes.scope: Source control; deployment pipelines are a separate release mechanism.

nodes.label: Governance domain
nodes.definition: A tenant-level grouping of workspaces and items with delegated administrators, tags and policy scope.
nodes.scope: Administrative boundary; a governance domain is not a workspace, a capacity or a security role.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish delegated domain administration from tenant-wide administration.

nodes.label: Fact-table grain
nodes.definition: The business meaning of one row in a fact table, declared before measures and relationships are designed.
nodes.scope: Model grain. Distinct from the grain of a query result; see concept:sql:grain.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Same everyday word as SQL output grain but a different scope.

nodes.label: Import mode
nodes.definition: A semantic-table storage mode that loads and compresses data into the model at refresh time.
nodes.scope: Freshness is bounded by refresh; model size and refresh cost are the trade-off.

nodes.label: Incremental refresh
nodes.definition: A refresh policy that processes a bounded recent window and keeps older partitions instead of reloading everything.
nodes.scope: Applies to supported model tables; partitioning and policy ranges must be defined.

nodes.label: KQL query
nodes.definition: Kusto Query Language, the pipelined query language used by Real-Time Intelligence and Eventhouse.
nodes.scope: Query language; not T-SQL and not DAX.

nodes.label: Lakehouse
nodes.definition: A Fabric data store that combines Files and managed Delta Tables with Spark and SQL access surfaces.
nodes.scope: Files and Tables are different locations with different discovery rules.

nodes.label: Data lineage and impact
nodes.definition: The recorded upstream and downstream relationships between items, used to inspect provenance and estimate the blast radius of a change.
nodes.scope: Dependency evidence; lineage visibility is not the same as data access and does not prove data correctness.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish provenance inspection from permission to read the underlying data.

nodes.label: Materialized lake view
nodes.definition: A persisted, refreshable view over lakehouse data with its own schedule, lineage and incremental-processing rules.
nodes.scope: Persisted transformation object; not an ad-hoc SQL view and not a semantic-model table.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish the stored result from the query definition and from the refresh schedule.

nodes.label: Medallion architecture
nodes.definition: A layered data design (bronze, silver, gold) that separates raw evidence, cleaned data and curated analytical output.
nodes.scope: Layering convention; layer names do not by themselves guarantee quality or governance.

nodes.label: SQL endpoint metadata sync
nodes.definition: The process that publishes lakehouse table metadata to the SQL analytics endpoint, with its own readiness and limitation states.
nodes.scope: Metadata publication; completion of a Spark write does not prove that endpoint metadata is ready.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish write completion, metadata visibility and query availability.

nodes.label: Machine-learning experiment
nodes.definition: Training, comparing and saving models in a Fabric data-science workflow, including experiment tracking.
nodes.scope: Model training and tracking; not a semantic model or a reporting layer.

nodes.label: Monitoring
nodes.definition: Run history, traces and telemetry that show whether items and refreshes succeeded, failed or were skipped.
nodes.scope: Operational observation; not a guarantee that the data is correct.

nodes.label: Spark notebook
nodes.definition: Code-based preparation and exploration of lakehouse data using Spark languages.
nodes.scope: Engineering surface for Delta writes; not the SQL analytics endpoint.

nodes.label: Object-level security
nodes.definition: A model permission that hides whole tables or columns from an identity, independently of row filters.
nodes.scope: Metadata and object visibility; not a row filter and not a substitute for RLS.

nodes.label: OneLake
nodes.definition: The tenant-wide logical data lake that stores Fabric items and exposes them through familiar storage paths.
nodes.scope: Storage substrate, not a query engine or a modelling layer.

nodes.label: OneLake security role
nodes.definition: A data-access role that grants table, folder or column access in OneLake across supported engines.
nodes.scope: OneLake data-plane role; workspace roles are a different control plane.

nodes.label: OPTIMIZE compaction
nodes.definition: A Delta maintenance operation that compacts small files; it does not by itself choose data layout for queries.
nodes.scope: Compaction. Different goal from Z-Order co-location and from V-Order write layout.

nodes.label: Partitioning and pruning
nodes.definition: Splitting data into files or directories by key values so a query can skip irrelevant data.
nodes.scope: Physical layout for pruning; not the same as incremental-refresh partitions in a semantic model.

nodes.label: Identity and permissions
nodes.definition: The identity, role and item-permission model that decides which operations and rows are available.
nodes.scope: Authorization layer; engine behaviour can still differ for the same identity.

nodes.label: Data pipeline
nodes.definition: Orchestration that coordinates data movement, transformation activities and control flow.
nodes.scope: Orchestration, not the transformation engine itself.

nodes.label: Pipeline parameter
nodes.definition: A run-time input that makes a pipeline reusable and can be passed from a parent to a child activity.
nodes.scope: Orchestration input; distinct from a semantic-model field parameter.

nodes.label: Pipeline reliability
nodes.definition: Retry, idempotency, replay safety and readiness checks that keep a pipeline correct across transient failures.
nodes.scope: Operational correctness; a successful activity run is not proof that the target data is correct.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish transport success from content validation and replay safety.

nodes.label: Relationship cardinality
nodes.definition: The one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many shape of a model relationship, including filter direction.
nodes.scope: Model relationship shape; join fan-out at query time is related but not identical.

nodes.label: Row-level security
nodes.definition: A filter model that restricts which rows a identity can read through a supported query surface.
nodes.scope: Engine-specific behaviour; Spark, SQL endpoint and semantic models can differ.

nodes.label: Slowly changing dimension
nodes.definition: A dimension design that preserves some history of attribute changes, commonly types 1, 2 and 3.
nodes.scope: History design. Type 2 adds versions; type 1 overwrites; type 3 keeps a previous column.

nodes.label: Layered security model
nodes.definition: The combined effect of tenant, workspace-role, item-permission, OneLake data-access and model security controls on what an identity can actually read or change.
nodes.scope: Effective access across layers; not a synonym for RLS, OLS, CLS, a workspace role or a sensitivity label.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish one mechanism from the effective access produced by every applicable layer.

nodes.label: Semantic model
nodes.definition: A Power BI/Fabric model of tables, relationships, measures and security that reports query.
nodes.scope: Container concept. Storage mode, relationship cardinality, DAX and security are separate concepts.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Do not use 'model' generically; a semantic model is a specific Fabric item.

nodes.label: Sensitivity label
nodes.definition: A Purview-managed classification that travels with a Fabric item and can carry protection settings, separate from item access.
nodes.scope: Classification and protection metadata; a label does not replace a workspace role or an OneLake data-access role.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Separate classification from authorization, and label inheritance from explicit access grants.

nodes.label: OneLake shortcut
nodes.definition: A named OneLake path that references an existing supported storage target instead of maintaining a separate copy.
nodes.scope: Reference object and the data it exposes are distinct; shortcut caching is a separate behaviour.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish referencing an existing target from copying, replicating or transforming it.

nodes.label: Snowflake schema
nodes.definition: A normalized dimensional model where dimensions are split into related sub-dimensions, trading joins for reduced redundancy.
nodes.scope: Normalized alternative to a star; the reporting trade-off is additional joins and complexity.

nodes.label: SQL analytics endpoint
nodes.definition: A read-oriented T-SQL surface over lakehouse Delta tables, with its own object and security behaviour.
nodes.scope: Read surface over lakehouse tables; not the same object as a Warehouse.

nodes.label: SQL schema objects
nodes.definition: Schemas, tables, views, functions and procedures as named database objects with separate permissions.
nodes.scope: Object model; a view stores read logic while a procedure stores an executable body.

nodes.label: SQL permission statements
nodes.definition: GRANT, REVOKE and DENY statements that add or remove explicit permissions on database objects.
nodes.scope: Explicit SQL permission rules; a DENY can override a grant, and REVOKE removes only the named rule.

nodes.label: Star schema
nodes.definition: A dimensional model with fact tables at a declared grain and conformed dimension tables around them.
nodes.scope: Model shape; relationship cardinality and filter direction are separate decisions.

nodes.label: Surrogate key
nodes.definition: A generated, stable key that identifies a dimension version independently of the business key.
nodes.scope: Version identity. A surrogate key is not the natural/business key and must not be reused across versions.

nodes.label: T-SQL query surface
nodes.definition: The T-SQL dialect and execution surface exposed by Fabric Warehouses and SQL analytics endpoints.
nodes.scope: Dialect and surface; supported writes differ between Warehouse and endpoint.

nodes.label: V-Order
nodes.definition: A write-time Parquet layout that trades additional write cost for faster reads by supported engines.
nodes.scope: Write-layout optimization; distinct from OPTIMIZE compaction and from Z-Order multi-dimensional clustering.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Distinguish write amplification from read acceleration and measure the workload before enabling it.

nodes.label: Data Warehouse
nodes.definition: A SQL-first Fabric store for structured analytical tables, views and multi-table transactions.
nodes.scope: Warehouse writes and T-SQL surface differ from lakehouse Files and Spark writes.

nodes.label: Fabric workload
nodes.definition: A Fabric capability area such as Data Factory, Data Engineering, Data Warehouse, Real-Time Intelligence or Data Science.
nodes.scope: Product workload; a workload name does not decide the correct item for a requirement.

nodes.label: Z-Order
nodes.definition: A layout technique that co-locates related values to improve data skipping for selected columns.
nodes.scope: Co-location for skipping; not the same as file compaction.

nodes.label: Aggregation
nodes.definition: Collapsing many input rows into summary values, with explicit choices about NULLs and denominators.
nodes.scope: SUM/AVG/COUNT semantics; aggregation changes grain.

nodes.label: CASE expression
nodes.definition: A conditional expression that maps conditions to values inside a query, including conditional aggregation.
nodes.scope: Expression-level branching; evaluation order and ELSE matter.

nodes.label: SQL data types
nodes.definition: The declared and inferred types that govern arithmetic, comparison, casting and division behaviour.
nodes.scope: Type precedence and integer division are correctness issues, not formatting details.

nodes.label: Date and time analytics
nodes.definition: Bucketing, truncating and joining time periods, including missing periods and event-time boundaries.
nodes.scope: Time semantics; a date bucket is not automatically a complete calendar spine.

nodes.label: Deduplication pattern
nodes.definition: Choosing one row per entity with ROW_NUMBER, DISTINCT or a key-based anti-join instead of arbitrary deletion.
nodes.scope: Business-record deduplication; physical compaction does not deduplicate records.

nodes.label: DISTINCT
nodes.definition: A deduplication operator that removes duplicate result rows after projection, not a row filter.
nodes.scope: Whole-row deduplication; it does not choose which duplicate to keep.

nodes.label: Row filtering
nodes.definition: WHERE predicates that decide which input rows enter the rest of the query, including NULL behaviour.
nodes.scope: Pre-grouping row filter; HAVING is a different stage.

nodes.label: Query output grain
nodes.definition: The meaning of one row in a query result, stated before joins, grouping or window functions are chosen.
nodes.scope: Query result grain. Related to, but not identical with, fact-table grain.
nodes.discriminatingContext: Homonym with concept:fabric:grain; scope differs (result shape vs model row meaning).

nodes.label: GROUP BY
nodes.definition: The clause that partitions rows into groups so each group produces one result row.
nodes.scope: Grouping key defines the grouped result grain.

nodes.label: HAVING filter
nodes.definition: A filter applied to groups after aggregation, unlike WHERE which filters rows before grouping.
nodes.scope: Post-aggregation filter; not a second WHERE.

nodes.label: Join
nodes.definition: A relational operation that combines rows from two inputs according to a predicate and join kind.
nodes.scope: Row-combining operation; cardinality determines whether rows multiply.

nodes.label: Keys and relationships
nodes.definition: Primary, foreign, candidate and composite keys that declare identity, uniqueness and referential links.
nodes.scope: Declared schema constraints. An unenforced declaration is metadata, not a guarantee.

nodes.label: Logical query processing order
nodes.definition: The conceptual order FROM/JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT that explains clause visibility.
nodes.scope: Logical meaning, not physical execution order.

nodes.label: Relational query mental model
nodes.definition: SQL as a declarative description of a result, with the optimizer choosing physical execution.
nodes.scope: Declarative meaning; the written order is not the engine's execution order.

nodes.label: NULL semantics
nodes.definition: The representation of an unknown or absent value, with three-valued logic and aggregate-specific behaviour.
nodes.scope: Unknown is not zero and not an empty string; COUNT(column) and comparisons treat it specially.

nodes.label: Ordering and determinism
nodes.definition: ORDER BY and the conditions under which a result order is deterministic rather than incidental.
nodes.scope: Result order; without ORDER BY, row order is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: Query population
nodes.definition: The set of rows a question is about before filtering, used as the denominator for rates and comparisons.
nodes.scope: Denominator definition; distinct from a statistical population although the two often align.

nodes.label: SELECT projection
nodes.definition: The projection and expression stage that chooses output columns, aliases and computed values.
nodes.scope: Projection happens logically after grouping; SELECT aliases are not generally visible in WHERE.

nodes.label: Set operations
nodes.definition: UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT combine compatible rowsets vertically rather than adding columns.
nodes.scope: Row stacking with compatibility rules; not a join.

nodes.label: Subquery and CTE
nodes.definition: A named or inline intermediate rowset used to stage a result before the outer query filters or joins it.
nodes.scope: Structural device; a CTE is not automatically materialized.

nodes.label: Text and pattern matching
nodes.definition: LIKE, pattern matching and text normalisation, including NULL and case-sensitivity traps.
nodes.scope: String comparison; collation and case behaviour are dialect-dependent.

nodes.label: DDL, DML and transactions
nodes.definition: Schema changes, row changes and the commit/rollback boundaries that make a data change safe.
nodes.scope: Data-change semantics; a committed change cannot be undone by rerunning the query.

nodes.label: Window function
nodes.definition: An analytic function that computes across a partition while preserving the underlying rows.
nodes.scope: Evaluated after grouping; cannot generally be filtered directly in WHERE.

nodes.label: Causation
nodes.definition: A claim that a change in one variable produces a change in another, requiring more than association.
nodes.scope: Causal claim; requires design or assumptions that correlation alone does not supply.

nodes.label: Measures of center
nodes.definition: Mean, median and mode, which summarize a typical value with different sensitivity to skew and outliers.
nodes.scope: Center only; says nothing about spread or shape.

nodes.label: Central limit theorem
nodes.definition: Under suitable conditions the sampling distribution of the sample mean approaches normality as sample size grows.
nodes.scope: About the sampling distribution of a statistic, not about the raw population becoming normal.

nodes.label: Confidence interval
nodes.definition: An interval produced by a procedure that would capture the parameter at a stated rate across repeated samples.
nodes.scope: Procedure-based coverage statement; not the probability that this interval contains the parameter.

nodes.label: Confounding
nodes.definition: A third factor associated with both exposure and outcome that can create or mask an apparent effect.
nodes.scope: Threat to causal interpretation; distinct from measurement error.

nodes.label: Correlation
nodes.definition: A measure of the strength and direction of a linear association between two variables.
nodes.scope: Linear association; a near-zero correlation does not rule out a strong non-linear relationship.

nodes.label: Descriptive vs inferential statistics
nodes.definition: Descriptive statistics summarize observed data; inferential statistics generalize from a sample with uncertainty.
nodes.scope: Two different claims: what the data show vs what the population may do.

nodes.label: Probability distribution
nodes.definition: A model of how values or outcomes are distributed, such as normal, binomial or Poisson.
nodes.scope: Distribution of a variable; the sampling distribution is a different object.

nodes.label: Type I and Type II errors
nodes.definition: False positive and false negative decisions, traded off through alpha, power and sample size.
nodes.scope: Decision errors; distinct from data-quality errors.

nodes.label: Experiment design
nodes.definition: Controlled comparison through randomization, blinding, placebo controls and explicit treatment groups.
nodes.scope: Design features that support causal interpretation; an observational comparison does not acquire them by labelling.

nodes.label: Hypothesis test
nodes.definition: A procedure that compares observed evidence with a null model and a stated decision rule.
nodes.scope: Decision procedure with assumptions; not proof of the alternative.

nodes.label: Outlier
nodes.definition: An observation far from the general pattern, which may be an error or a genuine extreme value.
nodes.scope: Investigate before removing; an outlier is not automatically invalid.

nodes.label: p-value
nodes.definition: The probability, under the null model, of evidence at least as extreme as that observed.
nodes.scope: Tail probability under H0; not the probability that H0 is true.

nodes.label: Population and sample
nodes.definition: The distinction between the full set of interest and the observed subset used to reason about it.
nodes.scope: Statistical population; related to but not identical with a SQL query population.

nodes.label: Statistical power
nodes.definition: The probability of detecting an effect of a given size under the alternative, driven by effect size, sample size and alpha.
nodes.scope: Design property; not a property of an observed result.

nodes.label: Practical significance
nodes.definition: Whether an effect is large enough to matter in context, as distinct from whether it is statistically detectable.
nodes.scope: Decision relevance; statistical significance does not establish practical importance.

nodes.label: Probability
nodes.definition: A number between zero and one describing how likely an event is under a stated model.
nodes.scope: Model-based likelihood; not a guarantee about a single observed outcome.

nodes.label: Sampling bias
nodes.definition: Systematic distortion from how observations were selected, not from random variation.
nodes.scope: Selection distortion; larger samples do not remove it.

nodes.label: Sampling distribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of a statistic across repeated samples from the same population.
nodes.scope: Distribution of a statistic; not the distribution of individual observations.

nodes.label: Sampling method
nodes.definition: The procedure used to select observations, such as random, stratified or convenience sampling.
nodes.scope: Selection procedure; determines which inferences are defensible.

nodes.label: Significance level
nodes.definition: The threshold alpha chosen before analysis that defines the rejection region and the accepted Type I error rate.
nodes.scope: Pre-declared decision rule; changing it after seeing results is a bias.

nodes.label: Measures of spread
nodes.definition: Range, variance, standard deviation and IQR, which describe how dispersed values are.
nodes.scope: Spread of observations; standard error is a different quantity.

nodes.label: Standard error
nodes.definition: The standard deviation of a statistic's sampling distribution, estimating how much an estimate would vary.
nodes.scope: Uncertainty of an estimate; not the spread of individual observations.

nodes.label: Accessibility and contrast
nodes.definition: Contrast, non-color cues, grayscale legibility and readable states that keep a view usable for more people.
nodes.scope: Accessibility duty; complementary to palette semantics, not a substitute.

nodes.label: Analytical task
nodes.definition: The comparison, distribution, relationship, composition or trend question the view must answer.
nodes.scope: Task precedes chart type; a chart is evidence for a task.

nodes.label: Annotation and context
nodes.definition: Titles, labels, units, source notes and annotations that make a view interpretable without guesswork.
nodes.scope: Context layer; a chart without units or source is incomplete.

nodes.label: Axis and baseline
nodes.definition: The choice of axis range and zero baseline, which changes how magnitude differences read.
nodes.scope: Bar length encodes magnitude from zero; line position does not carry the same baseline obligation.

nodes.label: Chart selection
nodes.definition: Choosing a chart form from the task, variable types and precision requirements rather than habit.
nodes.scope: Decision rule; not a list of banned charts.

nodes.label: Color palette semantics
nodes.definition: Qualitative, sequential and diverging palettes matched to the structure of the variable.
nodes.scope: Palette type follows meaning; diverging requires a meaningful midpoint.

nodes.label: Dashboard composition
nodes.definition: Arranging views, hierarchy and context so a dashboard supports a decision without excess cognitive load.
nodes.scope: Composition and attention; not merely a grid of charts.

nodes.label: Distribution plot
nodes.definition: Histograms, box plots, dot plots and density views that expose the shape and spread of a variable.
nodes.scope: Distribution task; bin width and summary choice change what is visible.

nodes.label: Part-to-whole
nodes.definition: Showing how parts compose a whole, where angle and area are weaker for precise comparison than position.
nodes.scope: Composition task; pie and polar forms are defensible mainly for genuine composition or circularity.

nodes.label: Relationship plot
nodes.definition: Scatter plots and related views that expose association, clusters and non-linearity between variables.
nodes.scope: Relationship task; correlation summaries can hide non-linear shape.

nodes.label: Scale
nodes.definition: Linear, logarithmic or other axis transformations that change how equal data steps appear on the page.
nodes.scope: Axis transformation; a log scale cannot represent zero and changes the meaning of distance.

nodes.label: Time-series plot
nodes.definition: A line or connected view for observations whose order is conceptually meaningful.
nodes.scope: Requires conceptual continuity; independent observations belong in a scatter plot.

nodes.label: Uncertainty display
nodes.definition: Showing intervals, error bars, bands or ranges so a reader can judge estimate precision.
nodes.scope: Display of uncertainty; must match the interval's actual meaning.

nodes.label: Variable type
nodes.definition: Whether a variable is categorical, ordinal, discrete or continuous, which constrains valid encodings and summaries.
nodes.scope: Property of the question and measure, not only of the storage column.

nodes.label: Visual encoding
nodes.definition: The mapping of data variables to visual channels such as position, length, angle, color, size and shape.
nodes.scope: Channel choice affects precision; position is generally more accurate than area or hue.

nodes.label: Visual integrity
nodes.definition: The duty not to distort magnitude, uncertainty or comparison through encoding, axes, cropping or framing.
nodes.scope: Honest representation; distinct from statistical validity of the underlying claim.

edges.claim: A join can multiply or preserve rows, so the intended output grain must be stated before a join kind is chosen.
edges.conditions: Applies whenever the join's cardinality is not guaranteed by a declared key; a verified one-to-one join may preserve grain.
edges.rationale: The SQL module verifies every JOIN against the declared output grain and a Fabric question asks the learner to predict fan-out from duplicate keys.

evidence.quote: Then verify that every JOIN and aggregation preserves or intentionally changes that grain.

edges.claim: Window functions are evaluated after the grouped result exists, so their behaviour depends on understanding aggregation first.
edges.conditions: For grouped queries; a window over ungrouped detail rows still depends on partition and ordering semantics.
edges.rationale: The logical processing order places window evaluation after GROUP BY/HAVING, which is why aggregate results are visible but WHERE cannot filter the window result.
